```{r}
#| label: setup
library(tidyverse)
library(predictmeans)

library(gridExtra)
```

## **2.1 Example 2.1 (Pg. 24)**

A field trial was planted to compare a seedlot derived from a seed orchard (SO) with one collected from a routine plantation (P). There were eight plots of each seedlot, thinned at seven years of age. Tree diameters at breast height (dbh) were measured at 15 years and plot means calculated.

### Data Info {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### Structure

```{r}
data(DataExam2.1, package="eda4treeR")
str(DataExam2.1)
```
#### Summary
```{r}
print(dfSummary(DataExam2.1, 
                varnumbers   = FALSE, 
                valid.col    = FALSE, 
                graph.magnif = 0.76),
      method = 'render')
```

#### Plot

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 7
DataExam2.1 %>% 
  ggplot(aes(x=seedlot, y=dbh, col=seedlot, fill=seedlot))+
  geom_boxplot(width=0.3, alpha=0.4)+
  geom_jitter(size=2)+
  theme_bw(9)
```


### Modelling {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### Model

```{r}
fmtab2.3 <- lm(formula = dbh ~ seedlot , data = DataExam2.1)
summary(fmtab2.3)
```

#### Residual Plot

```{r}
residplot(fmtab2.3) 
```

#### Test

```{r}
#perform shapiro-wilk test
shapiro.test(resid(fmtab2.3))

#perform bartlett test
bartlett.test(dbh ~ seedlot , data = DataExam2.1)

#perform levene test 
car::leveneTest(dbh ~ seedlot , data = DataExam2.1)
```


### ANOVA

```{r}
kable(anova(fmtab2.3), digits = 4)
```

### Predicted Means {.tabset .tabset-pills}


#### Mean Table

```{r}
predm_out <- predictmeans(fmtab2.3, "seedlot", meandecr=TRUE, bar=TRUE, adj="BH", prtplt=FALSE)
print(predm_out[1:4])
gt(predm_out$mean_table$Table, 
   caption = "Group: Letter-based representation of pairwise comparisons at significant level '0.05'")
```

#### Mean Plot

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 7
predm_out$predictmeansPlot$meanPlot
predm_out$predictmeansPlot$ciPlot
predm_out$predictmeansBarPlot
```

## **3.1 Example 3.1 (Pg. 30)**

We illustrate the recommended layout for data sheets with one of the trials conducted by the Australian Centre for International Agricultural Research (ACIAR) in Queensland, Australia (Experiment 309). This was a species trial planted in 1985; survival was poor. For our example we will examine only part of the data from this experiment. Five of the species with good survival have been extracted at random, namely Acacia, Angophora, Casuarina, Melaleuca and Petalostigma.

### Data Info {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### Structure

```{r}
data(DataExam3.1, package="eda4treeR")
str(DataExam3.1)
```

#### Summary
```{r}
print(dfSummary(DataExam3.1, 
                varnumbers   = FALSE, 
                valid.col    = FALSE, 
                graph.magnif = 0.76),
      method = 'render')
```


### Modelling {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### Model

```{r}
fmtab3.3 <- aov(ht ~ Error(repl/PlotNo)+seedlot, data = DataExam3.1)
summary(fmtab3.3)
```

#### Residual Plot

```{r}
residplot(fmtab3.3) 
```


### Predicted Means {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### Mean Table

-   Mean
```{r}
predm_out <- predictmeans(fmtab3.3, "seedlot", adj="BH", bar=TRUE, prtplt=FALSE)
print(predm_out[1:4])
gt(predm_out$mean_table$Table, 
   caption = "Group: Letter-based representation of pairwise comparisons at significant level '0.05'")
```

-   Pairwise p-values
```{r}
gt(data.frame(predm_out$`Pairwise p-value`, check.names=FALSE), 
   rownames_to_stub=TRUE, 
   caption = "The matrix has t-value above the diagonal, p-value (adjusted by 'BH' method) below the diagonal") %>% 
  cols_width(everything() ~ px(130))
```

#### Mean Plot

```{r}
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 7
predm_out$predictmeansPlot$meanPlot
predm_out$predictmeansPlot$ciPlot
predm_out$predictmeansBarPlot
```


### Remove three outliers

-   Outliers:
```{r}
DataExam3.1[c(28, 51, 76), ] %>% 
  gt(rownames_to_stub=TRUE)
```

-   Model:
```{r}
fmtab3.3N <- aov(ht ~ Error(repl/PlotNo/TreeNo)+seedlot, data = DataExam3.1[-c(28, 51, 76), ])
summary(fmtab3.3N)
```

## **4.1 Example 4.3 (Pg. 53)**

### Data Info {.tabset .tabset-pills}

Major seed distributors such as the Australian Tree Seed Centre (ATSC) routinely conduct seed viability tests so that, when seed is dispatched, the purchaser has an indication of the germination percentage of the seed. As part of the ATSC research program, a series of experiments was conducted in 1992 by Debbie Solomon on provenances of Acacia mangium to investigate methods of pre-treatment and loss of viability of stored seed. Each experiment involved six seedlots of Acacia mangium and four seed pre-treatments in a factorial design with three replicates.

#### Structure

```{r}
data(DataExam4.3, package="eda4treeR")
DataExam4.3$treat <- factor(DataExam4.3$treat, levels =c("control", "nick", "bw&s", "bw1min"))
DataExam4.3$contcomp <- factor(DataExam4.3$contcomp, levels = c("control", "Treated"))
str(DataExam4.3)
```

#### Summary

```{r}
print(dfSummary(DataExam4.3, 
                varnumbers   = FALSE, 
                valid.col    = FALSE, 
                graph.magnif = 0.76),
      method = 'render')
```


### Modelling {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### Model

```{r}
fm4.2 <- aov(percent ~ repl + contcomp + seedlot +
               treat/contcomp + contcomp/seedlot + treat/contcomp/seedlot
             , data = DataExam4.3)
kable(anova(fm4.2), digits = 4) 
```

#### Residual Plot

```{r}
residplot(fm4.2) 
```

## **4.2 Example 4.4 (Pg. 61)**

### Data Info {.tabset .tabset-pills}

An experiment supported by the Shell Company was planted at Toolara Forest Reserve near Gympie, Queensland, in February 1987 to study the effects of irrigation and fertiliser on four seedlots of Eucalyptus grandis. Because of the difficulty in applying the irrigation and fertiliser treatments individually to each
7 × 6 plot of trees, the experiment was designed as a split-plot, with main-plot treatments, irrig and fert. There were two replicates of four main-plots each with four sub-plots.

#### Structure

```{r}
data(DataExam4.4, package="eda4treeR")
DataExam4.4$seedlot <- factor(as.character(DataExam4.4$seedlot))
str(DataExam4.4)
```

#### Summary

```{r}
print(dfSummary(DataExam4.4, 
                varnumbers   = FALSE, 
                valid.col    = FALSE, 
                graph.magnif = 0.76),
      method = 'render')
```


### Modelling {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### Model

```{r}
fm4.6 <- aov(height ~ repl + irrig*fert*seedlot +
Error(repl/irrig:fert), data = DataExam4.4)
summary(fm4.6)
```

#### Residual Plot

```{r}
residplot(fm4.6) 
```

## **5.2 Example 5.1 (Pg. 68)**

### Data Info {.tabset .tabset-pills}

In 1985 species/provenance trials were laid out at six sites in Thailand as part of an ACIAR project extending over several years to investigate Australian multi-purpose tree species. The experimental design in each case was an RCB design with three replicates and the number of seedlots ranged from 30 to 42. Plots consisted of 5 × 5 trees with a 2m × 2m spacing. Plot summary files were constructed for the 24-month measurement according to the methods described in Chapter 3. Analyses were performed on the plot mean data at each site.

#### Structure

```{r}
data(DataExam5.1, package="eda4treeR")
str(DataExam5.1)
```

#### Summary

```{r}
print(dfSummary(DataExam5.1, 
                varnumbers   = FALSE, 
                valid.col    = FALSE, 
                graph.magnif = 0.76),
      method = 'render')
```


### Modelling

-   ANOVA
```{r}
fm5.2 <- lm(ht ~ site*seedlot, DataExam5.1)
kable(anova(fm5.2), digits = 4) 
```

-   Predicted Means

Site:
```{r}
site_mean <- Kmatrix(fm5.2, "site")$K%*%coef(fm5.2)
site_df <- data.frame(Site=rownames(site_mean), Mean=site_mean)
gt(site_df)
```

Seedlot:
```{r}
seedlot_mean <- t(Kmatrix(fm5.2, "seedlot")$K%*%coef(fm5.2))
gt(data.frame(seedlot_mean[, 1:9, drop=FALSE], check.names = FALSE, row.names ="Mean"), rownames_to_stub = TRUE)
gt(data.frame(seedlot_mean[, 10:18, drop=FALSE], check.names = FALSE, row.names ="Mean"), rownames_to_stub = TRUE)
gt(data.frame(seedlot_mean[, 19:27, drop=FALSE], check.names = FALSE, row.names ="Mean"), rownames_to_stub = TRUE)
```

-   ANOVA with Residual Mean_Sq 1040 and Df 208 (Table 5.3, page 71)
```{r}
fm5.2_aT <- anova(fm5.2)
fm5.2_aT["Residuals", c("Df", "Sum Sq", "Mean Sq")] <- c(208, 208* 1040, 1040)
fm5.2_aT$`F value`[3] <- fm5.2_aT$`Mean Sq`[3]/fm5.2_aT$`Mean Sq`[4]
fm5.2_aT$`Pr(>F)`[3] <- df(fm5.2_aT$`F value`[3], fm5.2_aT$Df[3]
, fm5.2_aT$Df[4])
kable(fm5.2_aT, digits = 4)
```

### Example 5.1 (continued) Page 78 {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### Book Way

## **8.1 Example 8.1 (Pg. 139)**

### Data Info {.tabset .tabset-pills}

In the early 1990s Khongsak Pinyopusarerk of CSIRO Forestry and Forest Products initiated a far-reaching study of Casuarina equisetifolia. This is a nitrogen-fixing tree of considerable social, economic and environmental importance in tropical/subtropical littoral zones of Asia, the Pacific and Africa. Provenance collections were obtained from 18 countries and, with this material, more than 40 trials were laid out in 20 countries. The number of seedlots included in each trial varied, depending on the suitability and size of the planting sites for the available material. One of the trials, in Weipa, northern Queensland, contained all the available seedlots and is the example used here.

#### Structure

```{r}
data(DataExam8.1, package="eda4treeR")
DataExam8.1$inoc <- factor(DataExam8.1$inoc, levels=c("1 week", "7 weeks"))
DataExam8.1$country <- factor(as.character(DataExam8.1$country))
str(DataExam8.1)
```

#### Summary

```{r}
print(dfSummary(DataExam8.1, 
                varnumbers   = FALSE, 
                valid.col    = FALSE, 
                graph.magnif = 0.76),
      method = 'render')
```


### Modelling {.tabset .tabset-pills}

#### Model

```{r}
fm8.2 <- aov(dbh ~ inoc*(country/prov) + Error(repl/(row:col))
, data = DataExam8.1)
summary(fm8.2)
```

#### Residual Plot

```{r}
fm8.2 <- lmer(dbh ~ inoc*(country/prov) + (1|repl/(row:col)), 
              control=lmerControl(check.nobs.vs.nlev = "ignore",
                                  check.nobs.vs.rankZ = "ignore",
                                  check.nobs.vs.nRE="ignore",
                                  optimizer ="Nelder_Mead"),
              data = DataExam8.1)
residplot(fm8.2) 
```


### Predicted Means

-   inoc
```{r}
predm_out <- predictmeans(fm8.2, "inoc", plot=FALSE)
print(predm_out[1:4])
gt(predm_out$mean_table)
```

-   country
```{r}
predm_out <- predictmeans(fm8.2, "country", plot=FALSE)
print(predm_out[1:4])
gt(predm_out$mean_table)
```

-   inoc:country
```{r}
predm_out <- predictmeans(fm8.2, "inoc:country", plot=FALSE)
print(predm_out[1:4])
gt(predm_out$mean_table)
```


## **8.5 Example 8.2 (Pg. 157)**

### Data Info {.tabset .tabset-pills}

In Example 7.1 we discussed a Eucalyptus clone trial conducted in Vietnam and described the experimental layout. The trial tested 56 hybrid clones of the interspecific hybrid combination E. urophylla × E. pellita (UP). These candidates had been selected from progeny trials of control-pollinated hybrid families; here we ignore the parental origins of the different UP clones.

#### Structure

```{r}
data(DataExam8.2, package="eda4treeR")
DataExam8.2$standard <- factor(DataExam8.2$standard, levels=c("0", "PN14", "SSOseed", "U6", "UG323"))
str(DataExam8.2)
```

#### Summary

```{r}
print(dfSummary(DataExam8.2, 
                varnumbers   = FALSE, 
                valid.col    = FALSE, 
                graph.magnif = 0.76),
      method = 'render')
```


### Modelling {.tabset .tabset-pills}


#### Model
```{r}
fm8.7 <- lmer(dbh ~ repl + column +
contcompf + contcompf:standard + (1| repl:row) + (1| repl:column) +(1| contcompv:clone), data = DataExam8.2)
summary(fm8.7, corr=FALSE)
```

#### Residual Plot
```{r}
residplot(fm8.7)
```


### ANOVA, adjusted $R^2$, Varcomp

-   ANOVA
```{r}
kable(anova(fm8.7, type=1), digits=4)
```

-   Adjusted $R^2$
```{r}
R2_glmm(fm8.7)
```

-   Varcomp
```{r}
gt(varcomp(fm8.7), rownames_to_stub=TRUE)
```

### Predicted Means {.tabset .tabset-pills}

-   repl
```{r}
predictmeans(fm8.7, "repl", plot=FALSE)
```

-   column
```{r}
predictmeans(fm8.7, "column", plot=FALSE)
```

-   standard|contcompf


#### Mean
```{r}
predm_out <- predictmeans(fm8.7, "contcompf:standard", atvar="contcompf", plot=FALSE)
print(predm_out[1:4])
gt(predm_out$mean_table$Table, groupname_col = "contcompf")
```

#### Pairwise p-values
```{r}
gt(data.frame(predm_out$`Pairwise p-value`, check.names=FALSE), 
   rownames_to_stub=TRUE, 
   caption = "The matrix has t-value above the diagonal, p-value (adjusted by 'BH' method) below the diagonal") %>% 
  cols_width(everything() ~ px(120))
```
